blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Altamont

items.t: Street-by-street boundaries are not verified; the area is generally the hillside above the Marine Drive / Queens Avenue corridor below Dundarave and the British Properties edge.
Where condo stock would concentrate in West Vancouver — the Ambleside waterfront and town centre and the Dundarave village edge — is outside Altamont.

Main streets: Marine Drive is the east–west waterfront route below the area, Queens Avenue climbs the hillside, and Taylor Way connects Marine Drive to Highway 1 (Upper Levels Highway); the Lions Gate Bridge is the fixed crossing to Vancouver.

Transit anchors: TransLink route 251 (Queens / Park Royal), operated as West Vancouver Blue Bus, serves the Queens Avenue corridor below the hillside, and route 250 runs on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge. There is no rapid transit and no condo node inside Altamont.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Altamont

items.t: West Vancouver tax timing: District of West Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026. At Altamont assessed values the Province's additional school tax can also apply — 0.2% on the residential portion between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

The name itself is unofficial. "Altamont" does not appear as a named neighbourhood in the District's OCP, Bylaw No. 4985, 2018 — a buyer searching strata registries, the zoning map or the OCP by that name will find nothing, because the District plans this hillside as part of the wider Dundarave–Ambleside side.

The density rules changed under the area on July 21, 2025. The Province directed West Vancouver to increase density in the single-family and duplex areas adjacent to Dundarave by December 31, 2025 — Altamont's lower streets are exactly that adjacency, so infill potential quoted from older material may already be stale.

Two hazard permits ride on hillside lots. Work within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface needs a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit, and work within 15 metres of the top of a watercourse bank needs an Environmental Development Permit; a Foreshore Development Permit applies to waterfront or coastal-flood-risk property on the lowest streets.

The seawalk below the hill dates to Canada's centennial. The Centennial Seawalk was built in 1967 and runs roughly 1.7 km east from Dundarave Park (150 25th Street, with more than 50 metres of sandy beach) to Ambleside — the waterfront amenity for an area that has no park confirmed inside its own lines.

The RS zone range is extreme. Minimum site areas in the zones that can apply run from 488 m² (RS5) to 8,094 m² (RS1) — two Altamont lots on adjoining streets can carry completely different subdivision and suite potential, confirmed only on the District's Zoning Map.
Westerleigh PARC is a rental residence — it surfaces in West Vancouver attached-housing searches but there is nothing to buy. (Standing correction supplied with this assignment.)

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Altamont

items.t: Street-by-street boundaries: Not verified — no District source read publishes them; the area is generally the hillside above the Marine Drive / Queens Avenue corridor below Dundarave and the British Properties edge.
Nearby areas: Dundarave (east), Caulfeild (west), the British Properties (north, uphill), Ambleside (south-east) and Chelsea Park (north-west, uphill).

Main roads: Marine Drive is the east–west waterfront route below the area; Queens Avenue climbs the hillside; Taylor Way connects Marine Drive to Highway 1 (Upper Levels Highway), and the Lions Gate Bridge is the fixed crossing to Vancouver.

Transit: route 251 (Queens / Park Royal), operated as West Vancouver Blue Bus, serves the Queens Avenue corridor below the hillside, running from Marine Drive at 25th Street to Park Royal via 27th Street, Queens Avenue, 15th Street, Mathers Avenue, Burley Drive, Kings Avenue, 11th Street, Fulton Avenue and 17th Street; route 250 runs on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver via Georgia Street, the Stanley Park Causeway and the Lions Gate Bridge.

Schools: School District 45 catchments are address-based and SD45 directs families to the school locator; no sample address inside Altamont could be taken from an official source, so the catchment for Altamont addresses is not verified — check each address in the locator. SD45 has no middle tier — elementary is Kindergarten to Grade 7 and secondary is Grade 8 to Grade 12. Nearby: Irwin Park Elementary (K–7), 2455 Haywood Avenue, in Dundarave; Westcot Elementary (K–7) at the foot of the British Properties; West Vancouver Secondary, 1750 Mathers Avenue.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Altamont

items.t: The governing pair is West Vancouver's own: Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 and Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, District of West Vancouver. White Rock's 2506/2220 pair is never attributed to West Vancouver.

If a strata townhouse is ever found on this hillside, the BC standard block applies in full: Form B diligence (Strata Property Act s. 59 — fees, amounts owing, approved special levies, CRF balance, insurance summary, with rules, budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page).

Rental and age bylaws: rental-restriction bylaws are VOID since Nov 24, 2022 — any directory "rentals not allowed" line for a West Vancouver strata is void for long-term rentals (short-term rentals can still be restricted); only 55+ age bylaws are valid since Nov 24, 2022 (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 + Regulation 7.01, exemptions expanded May 1, 2023). No Altamont complex exists to apply either rule to today.

Fee-simple reality in Altamont: the verified stock is fee-simple detached — NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees — governed by municipal rules (Zoning Bylaw No. 4662) and any registered covenants on title only. Secondary suites and a detached secondary suite are permitted uses in the single-family zones, subject to the bylaw's conditions.

Zoning numbers: Section 200 states minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, with RS6 using the area of the site of record; the ground-oriented dwelling rules state 4 dwellings maximum per lot, and 6 maximum if the site is wholly or partly within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop. The zone for a specific lot is on the District's Zoning Map.

Provincial density directive: on July 21, 2025, the Province directed West Vancouver to amend its OCP to provide increased density in the single-family and duplex areas adjacent to Ambleside and Dundarave (and at Park Royal–Taylor Way) by December 31, 2025 — Altamont sits directly above Dundarave, so infill rules on its lower streets are in transition and must be verified per property.

Hazards: an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank, and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface — both can apply on Altamont's hillside and creek lots; a Foreshore Development Permit can apply to the lowest streets below the hillside.

District taxes: West Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty applied to unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026. At Altamont price points the Province's additional school tax can apply — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% on the portion above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

Altamont is not an official District name. The OCP's structure is Ambleside, Park Royal, Dundarave, Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay — "Altamont" is a site/listing name for the hillside between Dundarave and Caulfeild, with no published street boundaries. Two agents can draw its lines differently and both be working from the same absence.

The seawalk below the hillside dates to Canada's centennial. The Centennial Seawalk was built in 1967 and runs roughly 1.7 km east from Dundarave Park to Ambleside, below the Altamont hillside; Dundarave Park, 150 25th Street, has more than 50 metres of sandy beach, a playground, washrooms and a seasonal concession.

The District's main indoor facilities are in Ambleside, not on the hill: the West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive, and the West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive — the library opened as a War Memorial, dedicated to those who served in the Second World War.

The hospital for the area is across the municipal line: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver (Vancouver Coastal Health), with the North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre at Suite 200, 221 West Esplanade, North Vancouver.

West Vancouver's 2021 Census population was 44,122 (Statistics Canada, 2021 Census Profile) — District context for a hillside pocket with no centre of its own; shopping inside Altamont itself is not verified (none confirmed on a District source), and Park Royal at Marine Drive and Taylor Way is the OCP-recognised regional shopping centre.
Utilities are metered and billed quarterly by the District — a carrying-cost difference from flat-fee municipalities that hillside buyers rarely budget for.

RS hillside lot fabric: detached houses on hillside lots in the RS single-family dwelling zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010. Section 200 states minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, with RS6 using the area of the site of record. The RS range that can apply here runs the full 488–8,094 m² ladder, so subdivision and suite potential differ lot by lot — the zone and minimum for a specific lot are confirmed on the District's Zoning Map. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Suites as lot value: Section 200 lists secondary suites and a detached secondary suite among permitted uses in the single-family zones; District building-permit guidance addresses detached secondary suites (coach houses) as a permitted form on these lots.
Bare-land strata: none verified

Serviced vs unserviced: District water and sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly by the District — the serviced position for District lots as the District states it. Septic or well servicing by street is not verified (Not verified item 11) — no street-level well/septic claim is made, and a specific lot's services are confirmed with the District.
ALR: parcel-level ALR status is not verified; no ALR split is stated for Altamont and none is invented.

Hazard-shaped land: this hillside's buildable value is permit-shaped — Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area ground (within 100 m of an undisturbed forest interface), watercourse setbacks (15 m from the top of a bank), and, on the lowest streets below the hillside, the Foreshore Development Permit Area. Gross lot area is not buildable area here.

No approved major project inside Altamont is confirmed on a District source — not verified: District major projects are listed at the District's major-projects page; none inside Altamont is documented.

Provincial density directive (July 21, 2025) — direction, not a rezoning: the Province directed West Vancouver to amend its OCP to provide increased density in the single-family and duplex areas adjacent to Ambleside and Dundarave (and at Park Royal–Taylor Way) by December 31, 2025. Altamont sits directly above Dundarave, so infill rules on its lower streets are in transition; the District's final adopted amendments as they apply to Altamont's lower streets are not verified (Not verified item 12). No lot is presented as rezoned on this basis.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Altamont

items.t: Municipality: District of West Vancouver, BC — Altamont is a residential hillside area of the District, above Marine Drive between Dundarave to the east and Caulfeild to the west; District-wide land use is guided by the Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 4985, 2018.

Boundaries: Not verified — no District source read publishes street-by-street boundaries for Altamont; the area is generally the hillside above the Marine Drive / Queens Avenue corridor below Dundarave and the British Properties edge. Nearby areas: Dundarave (east), Caulfeild (west), the British Properties (north, uphill), Ambleside (south-east) and Chelsea Park (north-west, uphill).

Roads and transit: Marine Drive is the east–west waterfront route below the area; Queens Avenue climbs the hillside; Taylor Way connects Marine Drive to Highway 1 (Upper Levels Highway), and the Lions Gate Bridge is the fixed crossing to Vancouver. Route 251 (Queens / Park Royal, West Vancouver Blue Bus) serves the Queens Avenue corridor below the hillside; route 250 runs on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver. Most Altamont streets are a hill walk or a drive from transit, the seawalk and Dundarave village. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Schools: SD45 (West Vancouver Schools) catchments are address-based and SD45 directs families to its locator; no sample address inside Altamont could be taken from an official source, so the catchment for Altamont addresses is not verified — check each address in the locator. SD45 has no middle tier (K–7 elementary, 8–12 secondary). Nearby schools: Irwin Park Elementary (K–7), 2455 Haywood Avenue, in Dundarave; Westcot Elementary (K–7), described by SD45 as at the foot of the British Properties; West Vancouver Secondary, 1750 Mathers Avenue.

Services are below the hill: Dundarave Park, 150 25th Street (50+ metres of sandy beach, at the east end of the Centennial Seawalk, built 1967, running ~1.7 km east to Ambleside); West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive; West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive; Park Royal, at Marine Drive and Taylor Way, is the OCP's regional shopping centre. No park, shopping or grocery inside Altamont itself is confirmed on a District source — not verified. Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, serves the North Shore.
District context: West Vancouver's 2021 Census population was 44,122 (Statistics Canada, 2021 Census Profile).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Altamont

items.t: Zoning + OCP (District): Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 (s.200 RS minimums in Sections 1–2; lot zone on the District Zoning Map) and Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018. An Altamont-specific local area plan is not verified (none confirmed). White Rock's bylaws (Zoning 2024 No. 2506 / OCP 2017 No. 2220) belong to WHITE ROCK ONLY and are never imported here.

SSMUH / ground-oriented density, as the bylaw states it: 4 dwellings maximum per lot, and 6 maximum if the site is wholly or partly within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop (Bylaw 4662, ss.620–630). Verify current infill zoning per property before marketing multiplex potential on the lower streets — the July 2025 provincial directive targeted the Dundarave-adjacent single-family/duplex areas, and the District's final adopted amendments for those streets are not verified.

Hazard development permits — the hillside rules: an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank; a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface — both can apply on Altamont's hillside and creek lots and can add geotechnical and permit cost to a rebuild. A Foreshore Development Permit is required for work within the Foreshore Development Permit Area (waterfront property or property at risk of coastal flooding), which can apply to the lowest streets below the hillside.

Strata block (no strata stock is documented in Altamont; stated for any strata lot form): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions. A listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules: no ALR ground is documented in Altamont (parcel status not verified), so no ALR rule is applied to an Altamont parcel here. Standing rules, for completeness only: ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; residence caps principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); farm class three-tier ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

PTT on land + the additional school tax that actually bites here: PTT general tiers 1% / 2% / 3% + further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000; first-time buyer and newly built home exemptions are home-purchase exemptions as BC states them — bare-land eligibility for the newly built home exemption: Not confirmed here. Budget for it in closing math where the residential assessment exceeds $3 million.

: District of West Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026; approximately 50% of the tax bill is collected by the District and remitted to other taxing authorities. Water/sewer utilities are metered, billed quarterly.

"Altamont" is a page name, not a District name. The District's OCP never names it — its structure is Ambleside Town Centre, Park Royal, and the Dundarave / Caulfeild Village / Horseshoe Bay village centres. A buyer searching District documents for "Altamont" zoning or boundaries will find nothing; the operative documents are the District-wide OCP 4985 and Zoning Bylaw 4662, read lot by lot.

The hillside's permit map matters more than its street map: the wildfire-interface line (100 m), the watercourse line (15 m from a bank top) and the foreshore area on the lowest streets each re-price what a lot can actually be built into — two lots on the same street can sit in different permit regimes.

Altamont's lower streets are the ones the Province named: the July 21, 2025 directive singled out the single-family/duplex areas adjacent to Dundarave — the ground directly below this hillside — for increased density by December 31, 2025, while the District's final adopted amendments for those streets remain not verified.

The seawalk below the hill is a centennial artifact: the Centennial Seawalk was built in 1967 for Canada's centennial and runs ~1.7 km from Dundarave Park to Ambleside — the waterfront amenity that anchors the hillside's value is public parkland, not lot frontage.

No market figure exists to quote for this hillside: West Vancouver is outside SnapStats coverage entirely, so any Altamont median, ratio or trend figure attributed to SnapStats anywhere should be treated as an error.

faq.a: A "condo" search result carrying an Altamont label should be checked for whether the property is actually in Ambleside or Dundarave.
faq.q: Are there any condos for sale in Altamont itself?

faq.a: In the District's centres named in the OCP — the Ambleside Municipal Town Centre and the Dundarave, Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay village centres — not on the Altamont hillside. The best-known waterfront building below the area, Villa Maris, is in Dundarave.
faq.q: Where is the nearest real condo stock?

faq.a: No. Secondary suites and detached secondary suites are permitted uses in the RS zones, but they are accessory to the detached lot — they are not separate strata lots and cannot be bought on their own title. The ground-oriented rules allow 4 dwellings per lot, or 6 within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop, still as one lot's ownership unless a future rezoning and stratification occur.
faq.q: Can I buy a suite or coach house separately in Altamont?

faq.a: Not for a long-term tenancy — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, whatever a building directory still shows. A short-term rental bylaw can still bind, and a 55+ age bylaw can still limit who may live in the unit.
faq.q: If I buy a condo in Ambleside or Dundarave instead, can the strata ban rentals?

faq.a: There is no strata, so there is no Form B, depreciation report or CRF to review. The equivalent checks are the lot's RS zone and minimum site area on the District's Zoning Map, and the hazard permit areas (wildfire interface, watercourse setback, foreshore) that can apply to hillside and creek lots.
faq.q: What replaces the Form B diligence for an Altamont house purchase?

faq.a: None verified — zero strata and zero fee-simple townhouse complexes on any source checked. The area is detached houses in the RS single-family zones. A "townhouse" search result carrying an Altamont label should be checked for whether the property is actually in Ambleside, Dundarave or Caulfeild.
faq.q: Are there any townhouses in Altamont?

faq.a: The Altamont hillside itself contributes none.
faq.q: Where is the nearest real townhouse stock?

faq.a: No. A detached secondary suite (coach house) is a permitted second unit on a fee-simple detached lot under Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 — no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.
faq.q: Is a coach house the same as a townhouse here?

faq.a: West Vancouver Schools (SD45) directs families to the school locator tool on its admissions page; catchments are address-based, and no Altamont catchment is confirmed here — check the exact address in the locator. SD45 has no middle schools: elementary is K–7 and secondary is 8–12.
faq.q: How do I find the catchment school for an Altamont address?

faq.a: Route 251 (Queens / Park Royal) on Queens Avenue below the hillside, and route 250 on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge.
faq.q: Which buses serve the Altamont area?

faq.a: The RS single-family dwelling zones in Section 200 of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010, with minimum site areas from 488 m² (RS5) to 8,094 m² (RS1), and secondary suites and detached secondary suites among the permitted uses.
faq.q: What zoning covers houses in Altamont?
